candidats.description: Travertine is a crystalline-textured, chemical sedimentary rock composed of calcium carbonate (calcite). It forms principally in cave environments and is the most common variety of speleothem (stalactites, stalagmites, etc.). Travertine also forms at some springs, either hot springs or cold springs. This example was recorded as "fracture fill" travertine. Locality: unrecorded

candidats.titre: File:Draufsicht quadratischer Natursteinfliesen aus nussbraunem Travertin Noce im Kreuzverband.jpg
candidats.description: Macro photograph of square natural stone tiles made of walnut to dark brown Travertine Noce, dimensions 20x20x1 cm. The background illustrates an installed surface in a straight grid pattern (stacked bond) showcasing the characteristically open-pore mineral structure. In the center, four loose individual square tiles are stacked rotated and offset to demonstrate the square format, the calibrated 1 cm material thickness, and the antique tumbled edge profiles. A striking light mineral inclusion on the top tile highlights the organic formation and authenticity of the natural stone. Author: Frank

candidats.titre: File:Depositi di travertino al colle san Nicola.jpg
candidats.description: E' visibile la zona di contatto tra le arenarie marine (substrato) erose con un intenso flusso in ambiente subacqueo, che ha formato sabbie carbonatiche a "stratificazione incrociata a festoni. " Superiormente inizia la deposizione dei travertini in ambiente termogenico (acque calde) con ossidi di ferro e manganese. Si tratta della prima struttura, nei travertini del versante adriatico, che indica direzione di flusso, ambiente, temperatura.
